I planted myself vineyards.”, web:Eccl.2.4, continuing through gardens, pools, servants, herds, and silver and gold) bound by the ethical dative li running unbroken across web:Eccl.2.4-Eccl.2.9 (sweep: 6 verses) and the mikol…lifnay…bi-Yerushalaim inclusio bracketing web:Eccl.2.7 and web:Eccl.2.9, and closes on the self-summary of 2:9-2:10, “So I was great, and increased more than all who were before me in Jerusalem.” (web:Eccl.2.9), before a fresh turning-formula opens the next row at 2:11.

boundary_rationale: A patterned companionship poem answers the solitary toiler of 4:8: טוֹבִ֥ים הַשְּׁנַ֖יִם מִן הָאֶחָ֑ד (oshb:Eccl.4.9, byte tier) — “Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their labor.” (web:Eccl.4.9) — develops across three parallel illustrations (falling, warmth, and resistance) before closing, “…and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.” (web:Eccl.4.12). The seam itself is warranted from both sides: 4:8 closes on the verdict refrain גַּם זֶ֥ה הֶ֛בֶל וְעִנְיַ֥ן רָ֖ע הֽוּא (oshb:Eccl.4.8, byte tier; this quoted span sits outside that verse's own ketiv/qere variant; the contiguous phrase gam-zeh-hevel returns 13 verses book-wide, with ve-inyan-ra appended at 1 verse), and 4:9 opens on the comparative טוֹבִ֥ים הַשְּׁנַ֖יִם מִן הָאֶחָ֑ד (oshb:Eccl.4.9, byte tier), a tov-min construction rather than a contiguous adjacency site (the plural tovim form recurs at 3 verses book-wide, only here verse-initial; the phrase min-ha-echad is book-exclusive, sweep: 1 verse) -- the refrain close against the comparative onset is what opens this row's own boundary.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping this stretch as monologue_unit (the parent's operative default) was considered and rejected: unlike the surrounding first-person narration, 4:9-12 carries no first-person verb at all and runs a three-clause conditional construction with three distinct lead particles -- כִּ֣י אִם (oshb:Eccl.4.10, byte tier), גַּ֛ם אִם (oshb:Eccl.4.11, byte tier), and וְאִֽם (oshb:Eccl.4.12, byte tier) -- not an identical repeated opener, a formal structure closer to the book's other patterned poems than to sustained autobiographical prose. saying_cluster was also considered and rejected: the four verses form one continuous, grammatically dependent illustration series -- each of 4:10-4:12 illustrates 4:9's own 'two are better than one' thesis, closing on a single capping image at 4:12 -- rather than detachable, independently-standing sayings, so wisdom_poem's patterned-poem category fits better than a cluster of sayings.

boundary_rationale: The mourning word “אֵ֗בֶל” (oshb:Eccl.7.2, byte tier), in the bare construct “בֵּֽית אֵ֗בֶל”, “house of mourning” (web:Eccl.7.2), opens the cluster at “בֵּֽית אֵ֗בֶל מִלֶּ֨כֶת֙ אֶל בֵּ֣ית מִשְׁתֶּ֔ה” (oshb:Eccl.7.2, byte tier), “It is better to go to the house of mourning than to go to the house of feasting” (web:Eccl.7.2). The same word stands again at the cluster's close, but with a prefixed preposition rather than a bare repetition: “בְּבֵ֣ית אֵ֔בֶל” (oshb:Eccl.7.4, byte tier from its own verse), in “לֵ֤ב חֲכָמִים֙ בְּבֵ֣ית אֵ֔בֶל וְלֵ֥ב כְּסִילִ֖ים בְּבֵ֥ית שִׂמְחָֽה” (oshb:Eccl.7.4, byte tier), “The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning; but the heart of fools is in the house of mirth” (web:Eccl.7.4). The bracket phrase as quoted at the opening collates byte tier against its own verse but only skeleton tier against oshb:Eccl.7.4, whose attested form carries the prefixed “in” that the opening's bare construct lacks. The driver that actually carries the boundary is the mourning word itself: “אֵ֗בֶל” / “אֵ֔בֶל” is word-bound identical at skeleton tier across the two ends and collates accent-stripped as a pointed form, and it is book-exclusive to this span (sweep: 2 verses book-wide, both inside the span, none elsewhere), matching neither excluded neighbour at any tier. Internal chaining is thin but real: the span's two adjacent pairs share one token apiece -- “ט֞וֹב” (oshb:Eccl.7.2) / “ט֥וֹב” (oshb:Eccl.7.3) (“good/better”) across web:Eccl.7.2-Eccl.7.3, and “לֵֽב” (oshb:Eccl.7.3) / “לֵ֤ב” (oshb:Eccl.7.4) (“heart”) across web:Eccl.7.3-Eccl.7.4 -- the honest thin-cohesion hold this cluster's confidence reflects. The middle verse, web:Eccl.7.3 (“Sorrow is better than laughter”), carries its own causal “for” clause on the same mourning-versus-mirth axis and sits inside the bracket rather than opening a new unit. The cluster is held apart from web:Eccl.7.1 (the mourning word matches it at no tier) and, less cleanly, from web:Eccl.7.5-Eccl.7.7: the fools word, “כְּסִילִ֖ים” (oshb:Eccl.7.4), recurs word-bound into web:Eccl.7.5 and also into web:Eccl.7.9 (sweep: 3 verses book-wide, web:Eccl.7.4, web:Eccl.7.5, web:Eccl.7.9), and a wise-root family bridges web:Eccl.7.4 into web:Eccl.7.5 and web:Eccl.7.7 across two attested spellings -- the plural “חֲכָמִים֙” (oshb:Eccl.7.4, sweep: 3 verses book-wide) and the singular “חָכָ֑ם” (oshb:Eccl.7.5) / “חָכָ֑ם” (oshb:Eccl.7.7) (sweep: 7 verses book-wide, 2 of them in this chapter). Both echoes are topic-level -- a shift from the mourning/mirth axis to the rebuke/song-of-fools axis at 7.5, then to an unrelated corruption saying at 7.7 -- rather than a repeated cohesion phrase, so neither pulls those verses into the bracket. A further rival stands over web:Eccl.7.3-Eccl.7.6 on the defective laughter spelling, “מִשְּׂחֹ֑ק” (oshb:Eccl.7.3) / “שְׂחֹ֣ק” (oshb:Eccl.7.6) (sweep: 2 verses book-wide, web:Eccl.7.3 and web:Eccl.7.6; the plene spelling adds 3 further verses book-wide), straddling this cluster's closing seam; but that envelope's own adjacent chain breaks at web:Eccl.7.5-Eccl.7.6, which share no word-bound content token, while this span's own chain holds at both adjacent pairs -- the mourning word, not the laughter root, is this span's driver.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating web:Eccl.7.1-Eccl.7.8 as one continuous cluster on the chapter's tov-opener anaphora was considered, since the anaphora is real (7 of 12 book-wide tov-openers stand in this chapter), but web:Eccl.7.1 shares no phrase with this bracket and web:Eccl.7.7 breaks the pattern outright, so a single mechanical span would erase real seams rather than argue past them. A closer rival, the defective-spelling laughter envelope over web:Eccl.7.3-Eccl.7.6, was also considered and rejected: its own adjacent chain breaks at the token-empty web:Eccl.7.5-Eccl.7.6 seam, while this span's mourning-word bracket holds at both adjacent pairs and is book-exclusive to its own bounds.

boundary_rationale:
This admonition spans the whole zone as one imperative/jussive-framed unit. The zone's directive forms cluster at its two ends: שַׁלַּ֥ח (oshb:Eccl.11.1, tier: byte), "send", opens the counsel, matching “Cast your bread on the waters” (web:Eccl.11.1); תֶּן (oshb:Eccl.11.2, tier: byte), "give", continues it, matching “Give a portion to seven, yes, even to eight” (web:Eccl.11.2); and the unit closes with זְרַ֣ע (oshb:Eccl.11.6, tier: byte), "sow", paired with the negative אַל תַּנַּ֣ח (oshb:Eccl.11.6, tier: byte), "do not let...rest", matching “In the morning sow your seed...in the evening don't withhold your hand” (web:Eccl.11.6). The three middle verses carry no second-person directive at all: v.3 opens a conditional protasis, אִם...עַל הָאָ֣רֶץ (oshb:Eccl.11.3, tier: byte); v.4 is a participial clause with a negated prefix-conjugation, שֹׁמֵ֥ר ר֖וּחַ לֹ֣א יִזְרָ֑ע (oshb:Eccl.11.4, tier: byte); and v.5 is a comparative declarative. This directive distribution, imperatives at the frame's two ends bracketing a directive-free middle, is what fixes the unit's own bounds rather than any split within it.

Three byte-grounded binders carry across the zone's internal seams. The negated-knowledge refrain interlocks the opening, middle and close: לֹ֣א תֵדַ֔ע (oshb:Eccl.11.2, tier: byte) collates at accent-stripped tier against כָּ֗כָה לֹ֤א תֵדַע֙ (oshb:Eccl.11.5, tier: byte), and אֵֽינְךָ֤ יוֹדֵ֨עַ֙ (oshb:Eccl.11.5, tier: byte) collates at skeleton tier against אֵֽינְךָ֨ יוֹדֵ֜ע (oshb:Eccl.11.6, tier: byte); each attested form is book-exclusive to this span (sweep: 2 verses book-wide for the know-negation, web:Eccl.11.2 and web:Eccl.11.5; sweep: 2 verses book-wide for the negated-existential form, web:Eccl.11.5 and web:Eccl.11.6), with all four sites falling inside this unit. The seam at 11:2/11:3 itself carries a repeated phrase, עַל הָאָֽרֶץ (oshb:Eccl.11.2, tier: byte) against עַל הָאָ֣רֶץ (oshb:Eccl.11.3, tier: byte), word-bound at skeleton tier (sweep: 7 verses book-wide, and 11:2/11:3 the only adjacent pair among them). A third binder ties the declarative middle to the closing imperative: the same triliteral sowing root (ז-ר-ע) stands in יִזְרָ֑ע (oshb:Eccl.11.4, tier: byte) and in זְרַ֣ע (oshb:Eccl.11.6, tier: byte), different inflected forms of the one root, not a word-bound identity, but book-exclusive to this span (sweep: 2 verses book-wide, both inside it). No byte warrant separates any internal seam that these three binders do not themselves cross.

Both outer bounds hold clean on content rather than chapter numbering: the back seam shares with the preceding verse only a causal particle, a function word, and that verse closes its own sentence zone (web:Eccl.10.20); the forward seam shares with the following verse only the object marker, and that verse opens the light-frame that begins the aging-allegory zone (web:Eccl.11.7).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading web:Eccl.11.1-Eccl.11.2 as its own admonition_unit, separate from the verses that follow, is rejected from the bytes: its two members share no content token with each other, while the negated-knowledge refrain and the repeated on-the-earth phrase both carry directly across the 11:2/11:3 seam that split would have to hold.
